inputs.share_count_basis: 90.4M shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2-26 balance sheet) plus ~0.3M unvested RSU/ESPP dilution (Q2-26 diluted weighted 91.1M vs basic 90.8M). Held FLAT: SBC (incl. tax-withholding repurchases) is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. Buybacks after 2026-06-30 are ignored on both sides (cash and count both at 30 June).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement SBC add-back $69.7M plus RSU tax-withholding repurchases (10-K Note 5: 0.1M shares at $247.80 = ~$24.8M; VRSN publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line). Withholding share count is rounded to 0.1M in the filing, so the $24.8M is +/- ~$12M.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.8 for a contract-protected registry with no cyclicality -> cost of equity ~8.3%. Debt (~$1.8B post-redemption, ~5% coupons, ~3.9% after tax) is ~7% of a ~$26B market cap, giving ~8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: the single-regulator/contract risk is carried by the 20% bear weight and its driver path, not by a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial (office/data-centre leases are small vs ~$1.2B EBITDA); no lease charge in flows and no lease liabilities in net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route), 10-year horizon. VRSN is a standard US operating company (registry operator for .com/.net), not a bank/REIT/holdco; routing table row 1. Negative book equity (-$2.25B) is a buyback artefact, which makes BVPS/equity-based models meaningless and is why the equity CAGR is not used. Unlevered flows: EBIT-based component build; interest expense is NOT in the flows and the debt is deducted in the bridge via net_debt. Net debt at 2026-06-30 = current 4.75% 2027 notes $549.3M + long-term notes $1,785.1M (incl. new 5.10% 2031 notes issued 26-Jun-26) less cash $840.9M and marketable securities $193.2M. The 2027 notes were redeemed 20-Jul-26 from the new issue plus cash, so net debt is unchanged pro forma (~$1.79B debt vs ~$0.49B cash). Company is a net borrower, so interest income ($26.5M FY25) is NOT stripped from owner FCF. last_fcf = reported FCF 1,068.3 - SBC incl. withholding 94.5 = 973.8 (reported FCF is post net interest of ~$50M pre-tax, so the unlevered equivalent is ~$1,010M). Buybacks ($881.6M FY25, $426.8M H1-26) plus dividends ($215M FY25, $0.81/qtr now) exceed FCF: VRSN is a full repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a convention. FY2026 guidance (Q2-26 call, 2026-07-23, per Analysis JSON): revenue $1.745-1.755B (+5.6% at midpoint), operating income $1.185-1.195B, capex $55-65M, GAAP ETR 22-25%, domain base +5.2-6.0%. .com wholesale fee $10.26 -> $10.97 (+6.9%) effective 1-Nov-26 (Analysis JSON; first increase of the current six-year window, which allows up to 7%/yr in its final four years, Oct-26 to Oct-30); .net $10.91 -> $12.00 effective 1-Mar-27 (8-K 2026-08-27). Owner-FCF year-1 sanity: rev ~1,750 x (74.0% adj EBITDA - 5.9% SBC - 1.6% D&A) = EBIT ~1,163, tax 21% -> NOPAT ~919, +D&A 28, -capex 60, +WC 66 -> ~953, vs FY25 owner FCF 973.8 (lifted by an unusually low 19% cash tax rate) - consistent, slightly conservative.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (equity is negative, -$2.25B, so equity CAGR is undefined)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR undefined (stockholders' deficit since FY2011 from debt-funded buybacks). EPS 5yr CAGR (4.5%) is depressed by FY2020's $7.08 which included a one-off tax benefit; EPS 3yr CAGR (12.2%) is buyback-assisted (~4%/yr share shrink) on ~5% revenue growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = FCF - SBC (cash-flow add-back; withholding only quantified for FY25). Owner-FCF CAGR (10.3% 3yr) slightly ABOVE reported FCF CAGR (9.95%): SBC is growing slower than cash flow, so none of the FCF growth is being paid for in stock. FY25 FCF was flattered by low cash tax ($202M, 19% of pretax vs 22.6% in FY24) and capex at 1.4% of revenue vs 3.4% guided for FY26.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 = guidance midpoint ($1.75B). FY27-30: .com price escalator ~7% taken in each of the four permitted years (Nov-26 onward, as VRSN did in all four of 2021-24) plus .net +10% (Mar-27), net of a volume slowdown to ~1-2% as the AI-era new-registration cohorts renew at mid-40% first-time rates. FY31-32: first two years of the next six-year window carry no .com increase -> volume only plus .net. FY33-35: escalator resumes at a partial rate.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC) FY25 73.8%, H1-26 74.3%, FY26 guide ~74%. Price increases fall almost entirely to profit on a ~fixed cost base, so ~0.8pp/yr expansion during the escalator years, plateauing at 77%.
base.wc_rationale: Prepaid multi-year registrations: deferred revenue ($1.45B) is ~0.85x revenue, so ~70% of each revenue increase arrives as cash ahead of recognition (FY25: deferred revenue +$80M on +$99M revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance is met in FY26 ($1.75B revenue) and VRSN takes the .com escalator in each of the four permitted years from Nov-26 (as it did in 2021-24), with .net at +10% from Mar-27. The AI-driven registration surge (new units +21% YoY in Q2-26, domain base +5.2-6.0% guided) fades as the large late-2025/2026 cohorts hit first-time renewal at mid-40% rates, leaving the base growing ~1-2% a year. Revenue compounds ~8% through FY30, then slows to ~4-5% when the next six-year window opens with two price-freeze years. Margins expand ~3pp on a fixed cost base; the business stays an annuity with near-zero reinvestment needs.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI-enabled business and website formation proves structural rather than a cohort spike: domain base growth holds ~3% a year while the full 7% .com escalator is taken every permitted year, .web launches with uncapped pricing and adds a modest new stream, and the 2030 .com renewal preserves the escalator. Revenue compounds ~9-10% through FY30 and 6% thereafter, adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 79%, and the market keeps paying ~22x for a contract-protected annuity.
scenario_narratives.bear: The single-contract dependency bites: the Department of Commerce/NTIA or ICANN, under political pressure on .com pricing, blocks or curtails the escalator after the Nov-26 increase (or the 2030 renewal removes it), while the first-time-renewal air pocket, new gTLD/ccTLD substitution (.ai/.io/.co) and app/social/AI-agent navigation shrink the .com base. Revenue growth falls to 2-3% a year, margins drift down a point as costs keep rising, and the exit multiple compresses to 15x as the market re-rates VRSN from compounder to capped utility.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because essentially all revenue rests on one government-controlled contract whose pricing terms are politically exposed. Base held at 55% because the escalator has been exercised in every permitted year since 2020 and the FY26 guide was just raised. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs both a structural (not cohort-driven) volume uplift and an unchanged escalator through the 2030 renewal.

valuation_philosophy.summary: VRSN is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF annuity: SBC (including RSU tax-withholding repurchases) is expensed and the share count held flat, so the ~$0.9-1.2B/yr of buybacks is the mechanism keeping the count flat rather than an extra source of value. The equity is the DCF enterprise value less ~$1.3B of net debt. The key value drivers are the .com price escalator (4 of every 6 years at up to 7%), registration volume, and whether the contract terms survive the 2030 renewal.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory: Commerce/NTIA or ICANN curtails .com pricing flexibility, or the 2030 renewal removes it (bear case).
Volume: first-time renewal of the large 2025-26 AI-era cohorts at mid-40% rates creates a 2H26-2027 domain-base air pocket.
Substitution: new gTLDs/ccTLDs and app/social/AI-agent navigation erode .com's share of new businesses over the decade.
Terminal dependence: the terminal value is most of EV; a 1pp WACC change moves value by roughly 15-20%.
Unverified inputs: the $10.97 .com fee from 1-Nov-26 and the raised FY26 guide come from the Analysis JSON (Q2-26 call), not from an 8-K seen in this build.
